claims.text: Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
A liquid-precursor impregnation-pyrolysis route can produce single-phase ZrB2 at a sintering temperature of approximately 1900–2100 °C.
Liquid-precursor processing provides intimate and uniform reactant distribution at the molecular scale.
Molecular-scale reactant mixing lowers the activation energy for ZrB2 formation.
Liquid-precursor processing permits densification of ZrB2 at lower sintering temperatures.
Liquid-precursor processing produces an ultrafine or nanoscale and compositionally uniform diboride microstructure.
The proposed route produces a dense ZrB2 ceramic with significantly reduced porosity.
Reduced-temperature processing through the liquid-precursor route limits grain growth.
Smaller, more uniform grains and a reduced pore network decrease pathways for liquid infiltration and corrosion.
Decreased liquid infiltration and corrosion mitigate hole formation during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Liquid-precursor-derived ZrB2 will have higher mechanical strength than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Liquid-precursor-derived ZrB2 will resist hole formation and component failure better than ZrB2 conventionally sintered above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 is characterized by extensive grain growth and higher porosity.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 is vulnerable to hole formation during liquid plating exposure.
The representative liquid plating bath causes corrosion and pitting that lead to mechanical degradation.
Liquid-precursor methods have successfully produced high-purity, ultrafine, uniformly distributed powders in other diboride systems at relatively low synthesis temperatures.
